If `tu.notification_level` is `NULL`/`nil` (as can happen in legacy rows, consistent with the existing `COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular)` usage elsewhere), Ruby will raise when comparing `nil` to an Integer (`nil > 1`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Direct tu.save! skips the upsert and notification_level_change MessageBus event publication that TopicUser.change provides, so the user's other open tabs won't update

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the PR updates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly. The diff shows that `TopicUser.change` is the method responsible for publishing the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)` event when `notification_level` changes. Because `unsubscribe` does not use `TopicUser.change` (or otherwise publish to MessageBus), other open tabs would not receive the realtime `notification_level_change` update that other code paths rely on.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Template registered as topic/unsubscribe doesn't match the Ember lookup topic-unsubscribe for the top-level topicUnsubscribe route, so rendering the page throws; template should be templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs (matching the companion view at views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6)

adjudication.rationale: The new Ember route is registered as a top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route (`app-route-map.js.es6`), and companion controller/view are named `topic-unsubscribe` (`controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`), which matches Ember’s dasherized lookup (`topic-unsubscribe`). But the template is added at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which registers as `topic/unsubscribe` (typically for a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route). Since `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` does not explicitly `renderTemplate` to `topic/unsubscribe`, Ember’s default lookup will not find this template and the route will error or render without the intended template.

In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, the unsubscribe block always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but `template_args` has no default `unsubscribe_url` (only `user_preferences_url`, etc.) and relies on callers passing it via `@opts`. The PR updates one caller (`app/mailers/user_notifications.rb`) and a spec to pass `unsubscribe_url`, implying it’s now required. adjudication_records.issue_text: topicUnsubscribe route (/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe) is shadowed by topicFromParams.fromParamsNear because it is mapped later and Ember matches in definition order, so nearPost='unsubscribe' matches and the unsubscribe page never renders; needs earlier mapping or a numeric constraint on :nearPost (and there is no guard in topic-from-params.js.es6, where nearPost is passed straight into postStream.refresh/closestPostForPostNumber)

adjudication.rationale: In the Ember route map, `topicUnsubscribe` is defined as `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, while `topic.fromParamsNear` is nested under the `topic` resource `/t/:id` with an extra single segment `/:nearPost`. The unsubscribe URL has *three* segments after `/t` (`:slug`, `:id`, `unsubscribe`), so it cannot be fully matched by `/t/:id/:nearPost` (which only allows two segments after `/t`). Thus `nearPost='unsubscribe'` shadowing does not follow from the diff’s route definitions/order. The `topic-from-params` guard concern would only matter if `/t/:id/unsubscribe` were handled client-side, but this diff’s Ember route is the slug+id form.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 'Stop notifications' toggle maps watching/tracking to regular instead of muted, so watching users still receive notification emails for replies/mentions despite link copy saying they will stop receiving notifications

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new “unsubscribe” action does not always mute the topic: it sets `notification_level` to `:regular` when the user was previously `> :regular` (i.e., tracking/watching):

```rb
if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
else
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted]
end
```

This behavior conflicts with the added copy/intent (“stop receiving notifications…” and “stop receiving notifications about this particular topic”), because tracking/watching users are merely downgraded to regular rather than muted. So the finding that the toggle maps watching/tracking to regular instead of muted is directly verifiable from the diff, and likely results in continued notifications inconsistent with the wording.

The diff shows `send_notification_email` now passes `unsubscribe_url`, and the `message_builder_spec` was updated to pass it too, implying it’s now required. However, the diff does not show any other call sites using `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, so the claim that other mailers (e.g. digest) will fail can’t be verified from this diff alone—though the risk is real if such call sites exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe flow fetches the full topic-view JSON (including cooked post HTML) via `PostStream.loadTopicView` for a page that only needs `fancy_title` and the notification level, and may deliver the same topic payload twice since the server embeds the full serializer via `store_preloaded` while the route doesn't consult `PreloadStore`

adjudication.rationale: In the new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the `model` hook unconditionally calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and returns a fully-populated `topic` record (`topic.updateFromJson(json)`), even though the unsubscribe page template only uses `model.fancyTitle` (via `stopNotificiationsText`) and renders `{{topic-notifications-button topic=model}}`. On the server side, the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` calls `perform_show_response`, whose HTML branch does `store_preloaded("topic_#{@topic_view.topic.id}", MultiJson.dump(topic_view_serializer))` and `render :show`. That means the full topic-view serializer is embedded into the initial HTML response for this route, but the new Ember route does not consult `PreloadStore` and will likely re-fetch the same topic-view JSON again, creating an avoidable extra request and payload. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:440-441 + topics_controller.rb:34: state-mutating GET endpoint with no token — any third-party page can silently change a logged-in user's per-topic notification level via , and email link-scanning/prefetching infrastructure will auto-GET the link and unsubscribe the user before they ever click it; should be POST or use a signed single-use unsubscribe key

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) that map to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, and that action mutates server state by toggling and saving `TopicUser.notification_level` (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`). It also explicitly allows non-XHR access (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`). adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController`, the diff explicitly adds `:unsubscribe` to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` and adds new GET routes to `topics#unsubscribe` (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). The new `unsubscribe` action mutates server state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. With `check_xhr` skipped, this state-changing behavior is now reachable via a plain GET request (including `.json` format) without whatever XHR-only protection `check_xhr` provided, making the finding accurate and security-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe performs a state-changing DB write on a GET request with no token or confirmation, making it triggerable cross-site via CSRF (e.g., `` with session cookie) and fireable by email-link prefetching/rewriting from scanners and mail clients, silently muting users without consent

adjudication_records.issue_text: The GET-based unsubscribe toggle is not idempotent on repeat fires: repeated requests cycle `watching → regular → muted`

This confirms repeated GETs can change state multiple times.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permanent state change (unsubscribe) is performed on an untokenized GET request: Rails CSRF protection doesn't cover GET so any third-party page can change a logged-in visitor's notification settings via an img tag, and email link prefetchers/corporate mail scanners following the link (and its 301) can unsubscribe users who never clicked; prefer a POST form/one-click endpoint or a per-user tokenized URL

Rails CSRF protections generally apply to non-GET verbs, so this introduces a CSRF/prefetch vulnerability: any third-party-triggered GET (e.g., ``) or mail-scanner/link-prefetch following the emailed `unsubscribe_url` can change a logged-in user’s notification settings without explicit intent. The email code explicitly injects `unsubscribe_url` into the unsubscribe link text, making accidental triggering more likely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The unsubscribe mutation happens on a plain GET with `check_xhr` skipped and no CSRF protection: (1) any web page can embed `` tags to silently mute a logged-in victim's topic notifications via sequential topic IDs, (2) corporate email scanners/prefetchers (SafeLinks et al.) auto-fetch the unsubscribe link without the user clicking, and (3) the action toggles rather than sets, so a reload or scanner-fetch plus a real click applies the downgrade twice (watching → regular → muted); fix by requiring a per-user/per-topic signed token and/or making the action idempotent (set to muted, don't toggle)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a state-changing `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that is reached via `get "t/:.../unsubscribe"` routes and explicitly skips `check_xhr` (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`). The action mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and `save!`s on a plain GET with no per-user/per-topic token in the URL or params. Since Rails CSRF protections generally do not apply to GET, this enables CSRF/prefetch-triggered mutation (e.g., ``), and the implementation is non-idempotent because it toggles between `:regular` and `:muted` depending on the prior level (`if tu.notification_level > ... then regular else muted`), so repeated fetches can flip state unexpectedly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Direct `tu.save!` in the controller bypasses `TopicUser.change`, skipping the `MessageBus.publish` of `notification_level_change` and the `notification_level_changed_at` bookkeeping, so the user's other open tabs/sessions never receive the level-change message and show stale notification state — inconsistent with every other notification-level mutation path

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)`, then `tu.notification_level = ...` and `tu.save!` (new code in `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`). Elsewhere in the codebase (shown in this diff), `TopicUser.change(...)` is the standard mutation path and it conditionally does `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, user_ids: [user_id])` when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set (`app/models/topic_user.rb`). By saving directly in the controller, the unsubscribe action will not publish the `notification_level_change` event, so any live UI relying on that bus event (e.g., other open tabs/sessions) can remain stale until a reload. The part about `notification_level_changed_at` bookkeeping is not verifiable from this diff, but skipping the `MessageBus.publish` is directly evidenced.
